## Lead review (2026-11-07 16:30)

- **Baseline check:** the new scorer reproduces EXP-003 exactly at G0 (68.53 paper / 66.17 live, 50,019 segments).
- **P2 caveat:** "no fill" at real time is a strawman — with ≥ 40% drops every 24-frame window misses > 2 frames and
  STG-NF (`is_seg_continuous`, missing_th 2) scores nothing (0.5). P2 passes only by construction.
- **Fair comparison (exploratory, not pre-registered):** P fill (G 8) vs the skip-and-reindex policy used in
  EXP-004/008 (same traces, same seeds), live variant, paired bootstrap over videos (1000):

| Group | s = 2 | s = 4 |
|---|---|---|
| SHT-L0 | **+2.77 [+0.87, +4.89]** (62.66 → 65.44) | **+5.61 [+2.53, +8.93]** (57.59 → 63.20) |
| SHT-L2 | **+3.72 [+1.63, +5.86]** (61.20 → 64.92) | **+5.52 [+2.34, +8.79]** (56.53 → 62.04) |
| UB-L0 | **+1.42 [+0.22, +2.50]** (54.69 → 56.11) | +1.76 [−0.17, +3.65] (53.97 → 55.73) |

  Caveat: the two policies also differ in how unfilled frames are scored (EXP-008 holds the last score; here they
  get the "normal" score), so the contrast is "fill at real time" vs "skip and re-index", not fill alone.
  Saved: `~/thesis-data/exp009/fill_vs_skip_paired.txt`.
- **Reading:** filling the frames a slow device cannot process — with causal prediction (P, no extra latency) —
  recovers 1.4–5.6 AUC of delivered accuracy, significantly in 5 of 6 cases and on both datasets. This is the first
  *method* in the programme that improves delivered accuracy on both datasets. Offline, filling helps modestly
  (SHT +0.9 paper, sig.; UB +0.95 with P G8, n.s.) and B ≥ P was wrong (P4 fail: causal prediction is as good or better).
- **Decomposition:** with reference-quality poses restricted to the people the edge detector finds, AUC is 69.23
  (vs 85.94): 96% (paper) / 91% (live) of the edge gap is *which people/frames are detected*, not pose quality.
- **Not a free compute saver:** a deliberate keyframe schedule (detector every 2nd frame + B) loses 1.8–2.7 AUC (P3 fail).
